a clear increase of transfer function entropy is observed for a few harmonics in the months preceding the Mw = 7.4 L’Aquila earthquake, suggesting a change of the conductivity (ordered or disordered) distribution in the lithosphere below L’Aquila area.

the 2009 seismic sequence was characterized by a clear pre-shock anomaly in the magnetic field, and that the observed magnetic anomaly could be explained by the deep fluid migration and/or by the variations in the micro- and meso-fracturing of the lithosphere below the seismogenic zone.
the 2009 April 6th Mw = 5.3 L’Aquila earthquake (Central Apennines, Italy) was preceded by a few months of anomalous magnetic activity in the frequency domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the magnetic field variations in the years before the 2009 seismic sequence in L'Aquila, with the aim of investigating possible precursory effects.
the study of a possible link between the magnetic transfer functions, their entropy, and the seismic activity.
the analysis of the geomagnetic field in the years before and after the main shock of L'Aquila earthquake.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2009 seismic activity in L'Aquila is associated with a complex system involving the crust and the uppermost mantle.
the observed magnetic transfer function entropy variations are likely to be related to deep processes, which may have contributed to the triggering of the L'Aquila earthquake sequence.

the observed magnetic transfer function entropy burst is a signature of a complex and non-stationary process, which is related to deep and lateral conductivity variations in the lithospheric mantle and/or crust under the L'Aquila area, and which could be associated with the 6 April 2019 earthquake.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the transfer function entropy analysis of the magnetic field components could be an effective tool to detect the onset of a seismic sequence, and to identify the time window in which the earthquake is more likely to occur.
the magnetic transfer functions, and their entropy, could represent a useful tool for the study of the pre-seismic phenomena.
the magnetic field is a good candidate for the monitoring of the deep and lateral geophysical conditions of the crust, in particular of the seismogenic layers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnetic observatory measurements can provide a useful tool in earthquake forecasting, especially when combined with other geophysical and seismological data.
the analysis of geomagnetic transfer functions can be a useful tool to investigate possible precursory signals of earthquakes.

the magnetic transfer function entropy analysis could be a useful tool in earthquake forecasting, and could help in the interpretation of the physical processes leading to the occurrence of an earthquake.
